title.zh: 卷四十六 雜傳第三十四: 趙在禮 霍彥威 房知溫 王晏球 安重霸 王建立 康福 郭延魯
title.en: Volume 46 Miscellaneous Biographies 26: Zhao Zaili, Huo Yanwei, Fang Zhiwen, Wang Yanqiu, An Zhongba, Wang Jianli, Kang Fu, Guo Yanlu
title.raw: 卷四十六 雜傳第三十四: 趙在禮 霍彥威 房知溫 王晏球 安重霸 王建立 康福 郭延魯 Volume 46 Miscellaneous Biographies 26: Zhao Zaili, Huo Yanwei, Fang Zhiwen, Wang Yanqiu, An Zhongba, Wang Jianli, Kang Fu, Guo Yanlu

sentences.zh: 趙在禮

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili

sentences.zh: 趙在禮，字幹臣，涿州人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili, courtesy name Ganchen, was a native of Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili, styled Ganchen, came from Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 少事劉仁恭為軍校，仁恭遣佐其子守文襲取滄州，其後守文為其弟守光所殺，在禮乃奔於晉。

translations.literal: In youth he served Liu Rengong as a military cadet; Rengong sent him to aid his son Shouwen in seizing Cangzhou; afterward Shouwen was killed by his younger brother Shouguang, and Zaili fled to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he served Liu Rengong as a military cadet. Rengong sent him to help his son Shouwen take Cangzhou. Shouwen was killed by his brother Shouguang; Zaili fled to Jin.

sentences.zh: 莊宗時，為效節指揮使，將魏兵戍瓦橋關。

translations.literal: Under Zhuangzong he was commander of the Loyalty-and-Restraint Army and led Wei troops to garrison Waqiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong he commanded the Loyalty-and-Restraint Army and garrisoned Waqiao Pass with Wei troops.

sentences.zh: 還至貝州，軍士皇甫暉作亂，推其將楊仁晟為首，仁晟不從，殺之；

translations.literal: Returning to Beizhou, the soldier Huangfu Hui mutinied, pushed their officer Yang Rensheng to lead, and Rensheng refused and was killed;
translations.idiomatic: On the march back to Beizhou, Huangfu Hui mutinied. The men pushed their officer Yang Rensheng to lead; Rensheng refused and they killed him;

sentences.zh: 又推一小校，小校不從，又殺之；

translations.literal: they again pushed a junior officer; the junior officer refused and they killed him again;
translations.idiomatic: they pushed a junior officer next; he refused and they killed him too;

sentences.zh: 乃攜二首詣在禮。

translations.literal: then they carried the two heads to Zaili.
translations.idiomatic: then they brought both heads to Zaili.

sentences.zh: 在禮聞亂，衣不及帶，方逾垣而走，暉曳其足而下之，環以白刃，示之二首，曰：「不從我者如此首！

translations.literal: Zaili heard of the mutiny, had not time to belt his robe, and was climbing the wall to flee when Hui dragged him down by the foot, ringed him with naked blades, showed him the two heads, and said: “Whoever will not follow me—like these heads!
translations.idiomatic: Zaili heard the uproar, belt still loose, and was over the wall when Hui yanked him down by the ankle, ringed him with naked steel, held up the two heads, and said: “Refuse me and your head joins these!

sentences.zh: 」在禮從之，遂反。

translations.literal: ” Zaili complied and thereupon rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zaili yielded and turned rebel.

sentences.zh: 在禮自貝州還攻魏，縱軍大掠。

translations.literal: Zaili returned from Beizhou to attack Wei and let the army plunder freely.
translations.idiomatic: Zaili marched from Beizhou on Wei and let his men loot at will.

sentences.zh: 是時，興唐尹王正言年老病昏，聞在禮至，呼吏草奏，吏已奔散，正言猶不知，方據案大怒，左右告曰：「賊已市中殺人，吏民皆走，欲誰呼邪？

translations.literal: At that time the Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan was old, ill, and muddled; hearing Zaili had come, he called clerks to draft a memorial, but the clerks had already fled; Zhengyan still did not know, and was raging at his desk when attendants told him: “The rebels are killing people in the market; officials and people have all fled—whom do you mean to summon?
translations.idiomatic: The Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan was old, sick, and half out of his wits. Hearing Zaili was near, he called for a memorial draft; the clerks were already gone. He still did not know—he was shouting at his desk—when attendants said: “The rebels are killing in the streets. Everyone has run. Whom will you call?

sentences.zh: 」正言大驚曰：「吾初不知此。

translations.literal: ” Zhengyan said in great alarm: “I did not know this at first.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhengyan started: “I had no idea.

sentences.zh: 」即索馬將去，廄吏曰：「公妻子為虜矣，安得馬乎？

translations.literal: ” He at once sought a horse to leave; the stable clerk said: “Your wife and children are already captives—where will you get a horse?
translations.idiomatic: ” He called for a horse. The groom said: “Your wife and children are already prisoners—where is the horse?

sentences.zh: 」正言惶恐，步出府門，見在禮，望而下拜，在禮呼正言曰：「公何自屈之甚邪！

translations.literal: ” In panic Zhengyan walked out the prefectural gate, saw Zaili, looked up and bowed down; Zaili called to him: “Sir, why abase yourself so!
translations.idiomatic: ” Terrified, he walked out the gate, saw Zaili, and prostrated himself. Zaili said: “Sir—why bow so low!

sentences.zh: 此軍士之情，非予誌也。

translations.literal: This is the soldiers’ feeling, not my intent.
translations.idiomatic: This is the army’s temper, not my wish.

sentences.zh: 」在禮即自稱兵馬留後。

translations.literal: ” Zaili thereupon styled himself acting military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zaili named himself acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉出帝時，以在禮為北面行營馬步都虞候，以擊契丹，未嘗有戰功。

translations.literal: Under Jin’s Emperor Chu he was made chief of horse and foot for the northern expeditionary camp to strike the Khitan, yet never won battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s Emperor Chu he was made chief of horse and foot for the northern camp against the Khitan and never won a battle.

sentences.zh: 在禮在宋州，人尤苦之；

translations.literal: When Zaili was at Songzhou, the people suffered especially;
translations.idiomatic: At Songzhou the people suffered under him especially;

sentences.zh: 已而罷去，宋人喜而相謂曰：「眼中拔釘，豈不樂哉！

translations.literal: when he was removed they rejoiced and said to one another: “A nail pulled from the eye—how could we not be glad!
translations.idiomatic: when he left they rejoiced: “A nail out of the eye—who would not be glad!

sentences.zh: 」既而復受詔居職，乃籍管內，口率錢一千，自號「拔釘錢。

translations.literal: ” Yet he received orders to take office again and therefore registered everyone in his jurisdiction, levying a thousand cash per mouth, and styled it the “nail-pulling money.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then orders came to return; he registered every household and took a thousand cash per mouth—the “nail-pulling tax.

sentences.zh: 」晉亡，契丹入汴，在禮自宋馳至洛陽，遇契丹拽剌等，拜於馬首，拽剌等兵共侵辱之，誅責貨財，在禮不勝其憤。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, the Khitan entered Bian; Zaili raced from Song to Luoyang, met the Khitan commander Zhuaila and others, bowed at their horses’ heads, and Zhuaila’s troops together insulted and abused him, demanding goods and wealth; Zaili could not bear the humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Jin fell; Khitan entered Bian. Zaili galloped from Song to Luoyang, met Zhuaila and other Khitan officers, and bowed at their stirrups. They shamed him together, squeezed him for goods, and he could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 行至鄭州，聞晉大臣多為契丹所鎖，中夜惶惑，解衣帶就馬櫪自經而卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhengzhou, he heard many Jin ministers were chained by the Khitan; in the middle of the night, anxious and confused, he undid his belt at the stable and hanged himself on the manger; he was sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhengzhou he heard Jin ministers chained by the Khitan. In the dead of night, frantic, he loosed his belt in the stable and hanged himself from the manger. He was sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖立，贈中書令。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu rose, Zaili was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu raised him posthumously to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 霍彥威

translations.literal: Huo Yanwei
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yanwei

sentences.zh: 霍彥威，字子重，洺州曲周人也。

translations.literal: Huo Yanwei, courtesy name Zizhong, was a native of Quzhou in Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yanwei, styled Zizhong, came from Quzhou in Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少遭兵亂，梁將霍存掠得之，愛其俊爽，養以為子。

translations.literal: In youth he met with military chaos; the Liang general Huo Cun seized him, loved his handsome alertness, and raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: War caught him young. The Liang general Huo Cun took him, loved his bright face, and raised him as a son.

sentences.zh: 嘗從存戰，中矢，眇其一目。

translations.literal: He once followed Cun in battle, was struck by an arrow, and lost sight in one eye.
translations.idiomatic: He fought under Cun, took an arrow, and lost an eye.

sentences.zh: 後事梁太祖，太祖亦愛之，稍遷左龍驤軍使、右監門衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Later he served Liang’s Founder; the Founder also favored him, and he was gradually promoted to commander of the Left Dragon-Prancing Army and general of the Right Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Liang’s Founder, who favored him too; he rose to commander of the Left Dragon-Prancing Army and general of the Right Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 預誅友珪，以功拜洺州刺史，遷邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: He took part in killing Yougui and for merit was made prefect of Mingzhou, then transferred to military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: He helped kill Yougui and was made prefect of Ming, then military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞遣梁叛將劉知俊攻邠州，彥威固守逾年，每獲知俊兵，必縱還之，知俊德之，後不復攻。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen sent the Liang turncoat Liu Zhijun to attack Bin; Yanwei held firm more than a year; whenever he captured Zhijun’s men he always released them; Zhijun was grateful and afterward did not attack again.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen sent the Liang turncoat Liu Zhijun against Bin. Yanwei held a year and more; every captive he sent back. Zhijun owed him and never struck again.

sentences.zh: 徙鎮義成，又徙天平，兼北面行營招討使，與晉軍相持河上，彥威屢敗，降為陜州留後。

translations.literal: He was moved to hold Yicheng, then to Tianping, and concurrently northern expeditionary commissioner; he faced Jin’s army on the Yellow River, was repeatedly defeated, and was reduced to acting commissioner of Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Yicheng, then Tianping, and served as northern expeditionary commissioner against Jin on the river. Defeated again and again, he was cut to acting commissioner of Shaan.

sentences.zh: 莊宗滅梁，彥威自陜來朝，莊宗置酒故梁崇元殿，彥威與梁將段凝、袁象先等皆在。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang; Yanwei came from Shaan to court; Zhuangzong set wine in the old Liang Chongyuan Hall; Yanwei and the Liang generals Duan Ning, Yuan Xiangxian, and others were all present.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang. Yanwei came from Shaan to court; wine was set in the old Liang Chongyuan Hall. Yanwei sat with Duan Ning, Yuan Xiangxian, and other Liang generals.

sentences.zh: 莊宗酒酣，指彥威等舉酒屬明宗曰：「此皆前日之敵，今侍吾飲，乃卿功也。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong, flushed with wine, pointed at Yanwei and the rest and raised his cup to Mingzong, saying: “These were all yesterday’s enemies; today they wait on my drinking—that is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong, drunk, pointed at Yanwei and the rest and raised his cup to Mingzong: “Yesterday’s enemies—today they pour my wine. That is your doing.

sentences.zh: 」彥威等惶恐伏地請死，莊宗勞之曰：「吾與總管戲爾，卿無畏也。

translations.literal: ” Yanwei and the others in terror prostrated themselves and begged for death; Zhuangzong comforted them: “I was jesting with the commander-in-chief—you need not fear.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yanwei and the rest pressed their foreheads to the floor and begged to die. Zhuangzong laughed: “A jest with the commander—fear nothing.

sentences.zh: 」賜姓名曰李紹真。

translations.literal: ” He bestowed the surname Li and the name Shaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: ” He gave the Li surname and the name Shaozhen.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙鎮武寧，從明宗擊契丹，明宗愛其為人，甚親厚之。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to hold Wuning and followed Mingzong to strike the Khitan; Mingzong loved his character and treated him with great closeness.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he held Wuning and marched with Mingzong against the Khitan. Mingzong loved the man and kept him near.

sentences.zh: 其後趙在禮反，彥威別討趙太於邢州，破之，還以兵屬明宗討在禮。

translations.literal: Later Zhao Zaili rebelled; Yanwei separately campaigned against Zhao Tai at Xingzhou, defeated him, returned, and placed his troops under Mingzong to campaign against Zaili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili rebelled. Yanwei campaigned alone against Zhao Tai at Xingzhou, broke him, returned, and put his men under Mingzong against Zaili.

sentences.zh: 明宗軍變，從馬直軍吏張破敗率眾殺將校，縱火焚營噪呼，明宗叱之曰：「自吾為帥十有餘年，何負爾輩！

translations.literal: Mingzong’s army mutinied; the horse-guard officer Zhang Pobai led the crowd to kill officers, set fires, burned the camp, and shouted; Mingzong shouted at them: “Since I became commander more than ten years—what have I owed you!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong’s host mutinied. Zhang Pobai of the horse guard led men to kill officers, burn the camp, and roar. Mingzong shouted: “More than ten years I have led you—what debt do I owe!

sentences.zh: 今賊城破在旦夕，乃爾輩立功名、取富貴之時。

translations.literal: The rebel city will fall any day now—this is your hour to win merit and seize wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel city falls any day—this is your hour for merit and gold.

sentences.zh: 況爾天子親軍，返效賊耶！

translations.literal: Moreover you are the Son of Heaven’s own army—will you turn traitor like the rebels!
translations.idiomatic: You are the emperor’s own troops—will you ape rebels!

sentences.zh: 」軍士對曰：「城中之人何罪，戍卒思歸而不得耳！

translations.literal: The soldiers answered: “What crime have the people in the city committed? The garrison only wants to go home and cannot!
translations.idiomatic: The men answered: “What crime have the people in the city? The garrison only wants home and cannot go!

sentences.zh: 天子不垂原宥，志在巢除。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven will not grant pardon; his aim is to root them out.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven will not forgive; he means to wipe them out.

sentences.zh: 且聞破魏之後，欲盡坑魏博諸軍，某等初無叛心，直畏死耳！

translations.literal: And we hear that after Wei is taken he means to bury all the Wei-Bo troops alive—we had no rebel heart at first; we only fear death!
translations.idiomatic: We hear that after Wei falls he will bury every Wei-Bo soldier alive—we never meant to rebel; we only fear death!

sentences.zh: 今宜與城中合勢，擊退諸鎮之兵，請天子帝河南，令公鎮河北。

translations.literal: Now we ought to join forces with the city, beat back the armies of the other circuits, ask the Son of Heaven to reign south of the river, and let you hold Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Now we should join the city, beat back the other circuits, set the Son of Heaven in the south, and let you hold Hebei.

sentences.zh: 」明宗涕泣諭之，亂兵環列而呼曰：「令公不欲帝河北，則佗人有之，我輩狼虎，豈識尊卑！

translations.literal: ” Mingzong wept and reasoned with them; the mutineers ringed him shouting: “If you will not be emperor in Hebei, someone else will! We are wolves and tigers—we know no rank!
translations.idiomatic: ” Mingzong wept and pleaded. The mutineers ringed him shouting: “If you will not rule Hebei, another will! We are wolves—we know no lord from lackey!

sentences.zh: 」彥威與安重誨勸明宗許之，乃擁兵入城，與在禮合，彥威獨不入。

translations.literal: ” Yanwei and An Chonghui urged Mingzong to promise; he was thereupon hustled into the city and joined Zaili; Yanwei alone did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yanwei and An Chonghui urged Mingzong to agree. They hustled him into the city to join Zaili; Yanwei alone stayed out.

sentences.zh: 明宗入城，與在禮置酒大會，而部兵在外者聞明宗反，皆潰去，獨彥威所將五千人營城西北隅不動。

translations.literal: Mingzong entered the city and set a great feast with Zaili, but troops of his still outside heard he had turned rebel and all scattered; only Yanwei’s five thousand men camped at the northwest corner of the wall and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong entered and feasted with Zaili. Troops outside heard he had rebelled and melted away; only Yanwei’s five thousand held the northwest corner of the wall and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 居二日，明宗復出，得彥威兵，乃之魏縣，謀欲還鎮州，彥威、重誨勸明宗以兵南向。

translations.literal: After two days Mingzong came out again, gathered Yanwei’s troops, and went to Wei county, planning to return to Zhenzhou; Yanwei and Chonghui urged Mingzong to march south with his army.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Mingzong came out, took Yanwei’s men, and went to Wei county, meaning to return to Zhenzhou. Yanwei and Chonghui urged him south with the army.

sentences.zh: 莊宗崩，彥威從明宗入洛陽，首率群臣勸進，內外機事，皆決彥威。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong died, Yanwei followed Mingzong into Luoyang, was first among the ministers to urge him to take the throne, and all inner and outer affairs were decided by Yanwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong died. Yanwei followed Mingzong into Luoyang, led the ministers in urging him to the throne, and inner and outer affairs ran through Yanwei.

sentences.zh: 彥威素與段凝、溫韜有隙，因擅捕凝、韜下獄，將殺之，安重誨曰：「凝、韜之惡，天下所知，然主上方平內難，以恩信示人，豈公報仇之時？

translations.literal: Yanwei had long been at odds with Duan Ning and Wen Tao; he therefore seized Ning and Tao on his own authority and threw them in prison, intending to kill them; An Chonghui said: “The crimes of Ning and Tao are known to the realm, yet the ruler has just settled internal strife and wishes to show grace and trust—is this the hour for private revenge?
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei had long hated Duan Ning and Wen Tao. He seized them on his own and threw them in prison to kill them. An Chonghui said: “Ning and Tao’s crimes are known to all—but the ruler has just ended civil war and means to show grace. Is this the hour for your revenge?

sentences.zh: 」彥威乃止。

translations.literal: ” Yanwei then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yanwei stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，乃赦凝、韜，放歸田里，已而卒賜死。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he amnestied Ning and Tao and sent them home to their villages; later they were still granted death by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong took the throne, amnestied Ning and Tao, and sent them home; later edict still gave them death.

sentences.zh: 彥威徙鎮平盧。

translations.literal: Yanwei was moved to hold Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei was moved to Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 朱守殷反，伏誅，彥威遣使者馳騎獻兩箭為賀，明宗賜兩箭以報之。

translations.literal: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled and was executed, Yanwei sent a messenger at full gallop to present two arrows in congratulation; Mingzong bestowed two arrows in return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouyin rebelled and was executed. Yanwei sent a rider at full gallop with two arrows in congratulation; Mingzong returned two arrows.

sentences.zh: 夷狄之法，起兵令眾，以傳箭為號令，然非下得施於上也。

translations.literal: By barbarian custom, to muster troops for war they used passing arrows as signals, yet subordinates could not impose this on superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Among barbarians, arrows passed hand to hand were the signal to muster—but a subordinate could not impose that on a superior.

sentences.zh: 明宗本出夷狄，而彥威武人，君臣皆不知禮，動多此類。

translations.literal: Mingzong came from barbarian stock and Yanwei was a military man; ruler and minister both knew little of ritual, and their acts were often of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong came from barbarian stock; Yanwei was a soldier. Neither knew ritual; their acts were often like this.

sentences.zh: 然彥威客有淳於晏者，登州人也，少舉明經及第，遭世亂，依彥威，自彥威為偏裨時已從之。

translations.literal: Yet Yanwei had a retainer, Chunyu Yan of Dengzhou, who in youth passed the classics examination with honors, met with the age’s chaos, and attached himself to Yanwei, following him from the time Yanwei was still a junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei kept a retainer, Chunyu Yan of Dengzhou, who had passed the classics examination in youth, met the age’s chaos, and followed Yanwei from his days as a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 彥威嘗戰敗脫身走，麾下兵無從者，獨晏徒步以一劍從之榛棘間以免。

translations.literal: Yanwei once fled a lost battle with no troops following; only Yan walked on foot with a single sword through thorn scrub and so escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei once fled a rout with no one behind him; only Yan walked through thorns with one sword and kept him alive.

sentences.zh: 彥威高其義，所歷方鎮，常辟以自從，至其家事無大小，皆決於晏，彥威以故得少過失。

translations.literal: Yanwei honored his loyalty; in every circuit he held he always took Yan as aide and followed him; great and small household affairs were all decided by Yan, and Yanwei therefore had few faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei honored his loyalty; in every post he kept Yan at his side; household affairs great and small ran through Yan, and Yanwei therefore stumbled rarely.

sentences.zh: 當時諸鎮辟召寮屬，皆以晏為法。

translations.literal: At that time every circuit, in recruiting staff, took Yan as the model.
translations.idiomatic: Every circuit recruiting staff took Yan as the model.

sentences.zh: 天成三年冬，彥威卒於鎮。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year of Tiancheng, Yanwei died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, Tiancheng 3: Yanwei died in his post.

sentences.zh: 是時，明宗方獵於近郊，青州馳騎奏彥威卒，明宗涕泣還宮，輟朝，仍終其月不舉樂，贈彥威太師，謚曰忠武。

translations.literal: At that time Mingzong was hunting near the capital; Qingzhou sent riders reporting Yanwei’s death; Mingzong wept and returned to the palace, suspended court, and for the whole month did not hold music; Yanwei was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was hunting near the capital. Qingzhou sent riders with word of Yanwei’s death. Mingzong wept, returned to the palace, suspended court, and for the whole month held no music. They made him Grand Preceptor posthumously, styled Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: ○房知溫

translations.literal: ○ Fang Zhiwen
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhiwen

sentences.zh: 房知溫，字伯玉，兗州瑕丘人也。

translations.literal: Fang Zhiwen, courtesy name Boyu, was a native of Xiaqiu in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhiwen, styled Boyu, came from Xiaqiu in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少以勇力為赤甲都官健，後隸魏州馬鬥軍，稍遷親隨軍指揮使。

translations.literal: In youth, for courage and strength, he was a Red-Armor metropolitan guard; later he entered the Wei Horse-Fighting Army and was gradually promoted to commander of the personal following army.
translations.idiomatic: Young, for strength he served as a Red-Armor metropolitan guard; later he joined the Wei Horse-Fighting Army and rose to commander of the personal following.

sentences.zh: 莊宗取魏博，得知溫，賜姓李氏，名曰紹英，以為澶州刺史，歷曹、貝二州刺史，戍瓦橋關。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took Wei-Bo he came to know Zhiwen, bestowed the surname Li and the name Shaoying, made him prefect of Tan, then in turn prefect of Cao and Bei, and garrisoned Waqiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong took Wei-Bo and knew Zhiwen, gave him the Li surname and the name Shaoying, made him prefect of Tan, then Cao and Bei in turn, and garrisoned Waqiao Pass.

sentences.zh: 明宗自魏反兵南向，知溫首馳赴之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong turned rebel in Wei and marched his army south, Zhiwen was first to gallop to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong rebelled in Wei and marched south, Zhiwen was first to gallop to him.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，拜泰寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was made military commissioner of the Taining Army.
translations.idiomatic: Tiancheng 1: he was made military commissioner of Taining.

sentences.zh: 明年，為北面招討使，屯於盧臺。

translations.literal: The next year he was northern expeditionary commissioner and encamped at Lutai.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he was northern expeditionary commissioner at Lutai.

sentences.zh: 明宗遣烏震往代知溫還鎮，其戍卒效節軍將龍至等攻震殺之。

translations.literal: Mingzong sent Wu Zhen to replace Zhiwen and return to his post; the garrison’s Loyalty-and-Restraint officer Long Zhi and others attacked and killed Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent Wu Zhen to replace Zhiwen and return to his post. The garrison’s Loyalty-and-Restraint officer Long Zhi and others attacked and killed Zhen.

sentences.zh: 效節，魏州軍也。

translations.literal: Loyalty-and-Restraint was the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty-and-Restraint was the Wei army.

sentences.zh: 魏州自羅紹威誅衙軍，楊師厚為節度使，復置銀槍效節軍。

translations.literal: Since Luo Shaowei executed the yamen army and Yang Shihou became military commissioner, he re-established the Silver Spear Loyalty-and-Restraint Army.
translations.idiomatic: Since Luo Shaowei killed the yamen army and Yang Shihou became commissioner, he re-established the Silver Spear Loyalty-and-Restraint Army.

sentences.zh: 當梁末帝時，師厚幾為梁患。

translations.literal: In Liang’s Last Emperor’s time Shihou nearly became a trouble to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang’s Last Emperor, Shihou nearly became Liang’s trouble.

sentences.zh: 師厚卒，以賀德倫代之。

translations.literal: When Shihou died, He Delun replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou died; He Delun replaced him.

sentences.zh: 末帝患魏軍強難制，與趙巖等謀分相、魏為兩鎮，魏軍由此作亂，劫德倫叛梁而降晉，梁遂失河北。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor feared the Wei army’s strength was hard to control; with Zhao Yan and others he plotted to split Xiang and Wei into two circuits; the Wei army therefore mutinied, seized Delun, rebelled against Liang and surrendered to Jin, and Liang thereby lost Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor feared the Wei host; with Zhao Yan and others he plotted to split Xiang and Wei into two circuits. The Wei army mutinied, seized Delun, left Liang for Jin, and Liang lost Hebei.

sentences.zh: 莊宗自得魏兵，與梁戰河上，數有功，許其軍以滅梁而厚賞。

translations.literal: Once Zhuangzong had the Wei troops, he fought Liang on the river and won merit again and again, promising the army rich reward when Liang was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong took the Wei troops, fought Liang on the river, won again and again, and promised rich reward when Liang fell.

sentences.zh: 及梁亡，魏軍雖數賜與，而驕縱無厭，常懷怨望；

translations.literal: When Liang fell the Wei army was repeatedly rewarded, yet arrogant and insatiable, always nursing resentment;
translations.idiomatic: Liang fell; the Wei army was rewarded again and again, yet grew arrogant and insatiable and nursed resentment;

sentences.zh: 皇甫暉之亂，劫趙在禮入魏，皆此軍也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Hui’s mutiny, seizing Zhao Zaili into Wei—all were this army.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui’s mutiny that seized Zhao Zaili in Wei—all that army.

sentences.zh: 明宗入立，在禮鎮天雄軍，以魏軍素驕，常懼禍，不遑居，陰遣人訴於明宗，求解去。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Zaili held the Tianxiong Army; because the Wei army had long been arrogant he constantly feared disaster, could not rest easy in his post, and secretly sent men to plead with Mingzong to be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong took the throne; Zaili held Tianxiong. The Wei army had long been arrogant; he lived in fear, could not rest, and secretly begged Mingzong to let him go.

sentences.zh: 明宗乃以皇子從榮代在禮，而遣魏效節九指揮北戍盧臺。

translations.literal: Mingzong therefore put his son Congrong in Zaili’s place and sent the nine Loyalty-and-Restraint commanders of Wei north to garrison Lutai.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong put his son Congrong in Zaili’s place and sent the nine Wei Loyalty-and-Restraint commanders north to Lutai.

sentences.zh: 軍發之日，不給兵甲，惟以長竿系旗幟以表隊伍，軍士頗自疑惑。

translations.literal: On the day the army marched out they were given no armor or weapons—only long poles with banners to mark the ranks—and the soldiers were much unsettled in mind.
translations.idiomatic: On the march day they were given no armor or arms—only long poles with banners to mark ranks—and the men were deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 明年，明宗遣烏震代知溫戍，而知溫意尤不樂。

translations.literal: The next year Mingzong sent Wu Zhen to replace Zhiwen on garrison duty, and Zhiwen was especially displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Mingzong sent Wu Zhen to replace Zhiwen on garrison duty; Zhiwen was especially displeased.

sentences.zh: 盧臺戍軍夾水東西為兩寨，震初至，與知溫會東寨，方博，效節軍亂，噪於門外，知溫即乘馬而出。

translations.literal: The Lutai garrison split east and west of the water into two camps; when Zhen first arrived he met Zhiwen in the eastern camp; they were gambling when the Loyalty-and-Restraint army mutinied and shouted outside the gate; Zhiwen at once mounted and went out.
translations.idiomatic: The Lutai garrison split into eastern and western camps across the water. Zhen arrived and met Zhiwen in the east camp; they were gambling when the Loyalty-and-Restraint men mutinied and roared at the gate. Zhiwen mounted at once.

sentences.zh: 亂軍擊殺震，執轡留知溫，知溫紿曰：「騎兵皆在西寨，今獨步軍，恐無能為也。

translations.literal: The mutineers killed Zhen and seized the reins to hold Zhiwen; Zhiwen deceived them, saying: “The cavalry are all in the western camp; now there are only foot soldiers—I fear they can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers killed Zhen and seized Zhiwen’s reins. Zhiwen lied: “All the cavalry are in the west camp. You have only foot soldiers—I fear you can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 」知溫即躍馬登舟渡河入西寨，以騎軍盡殺亂者。

translations.literal: ” Zhiwen at once leaped on his horse, boarded a boat, crossed the river into the western camp, and with the cavalry killed all the mutineers.
translations.idiomatic: ” He leaped to his horse, boarded a boat, crossed to the west camp, and the cavalry killed every mutineer.

sentences.zh: 明宗下詔，悉誅其家屬於魏州，凡九指揮三千餘家數萬口，驅至漳水上殺之，漳水為之變色。

translations.literal: Mingzong issued an edict to execute all their families in Wei—nine commanders, more than three thousand households, tens of thousands of mouths, driven to the Zhang River and killed; the Zhang’s water changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong ordered every family executed in Wei—nine commanders, more than three thousand households, tens of thousands driven to the Zhang River and killed; the Zhang ran red.

sentences.zh: 魏之驕兵，於是而盡。

translations.literal: Wei’s arrogant troops were thereby ended.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s arrogant troops ended there.

sentences.zh: 明宗知變自知溫起，釋而不問，徙鎮武寧，加兼侍中，歷鎮天平、平盧。

translations.literal: Mingzong knew the mutiny rose from Zhiwen and released him without inquiry; he was moved to Wuning, further made concurrent Palace Attendant, and in turn held Tianping and Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong knew the mutiny rose from Zhiwen and let it pass; he moved him to Wuning, made him Palace Attendant, and later Tianping and Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 初，明宗為北面招討使，而知溫為副使，廢帝時以裨將事知溫甚謹，後因杯酒失意。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mingzong was northern expeditionary commissioner, Zhiwen was his deputy; under the Deposed Emperor he served Zhiwen as a junior officer with great deference, but later lost favor over a cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Mingzong was northern expeditionary commissioner and Zhiwen his deputy. Under the Deposed Emperor he served Zhiwen as junior officer with great deference; later a cup of wine cost him favor.

sentences.zh: 及廢帝起兵鳳翔，湣帝出奔，知溫乘間有窺覦之意，謂其司馬李沖曰：「吾有錢數屋，養兵數千，因時建義，功必有成。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor raised troops at Fengxiang and the Lamented Emperor fled, Zhiwen seized the moment with designs of his own and told his chief administrator Li Chong: “I have money enough to fill several rooms and thousands of troops under arms; if I seize the moment and raise a righteous cause, merit is sure to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor raised troops at Fengxiang and the Lamented Emperor fled, Zhiwen saw his chance and told his chief administrator Li Chong: “I have money to fill several rooms and thousands under arms. Seize the moment, raise a righteous cause, and merit is sure.

sentences.zh: 」沖曰：「今天子孱弱，上下離心，潞王兵威甚盛，事未可知，沖請懷表而西以覘之。

translations.literal: ” Chong said: “Today the Son of Heaven is weak; above and below are divided; the Prince of Lu’s military might is very great; the outcome is unknown—I beg to carry a memorial west and observe.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chong said: “The Son of Heaven is weak; the court is split; the Prince of Lu’s host is very strong—the outcome is unknown. Let me carry a memorial west and see.

sentences.zh: 」及沖至京師，廢帝已入立，沖即奉表稱賀，還勸知溫入朝，廢帝慰勞之甚厚。

translations.literal: ” When Chong reached the capital the Deposed Emperor had already taken the throne; Chong at once presented a memorial of congratulation, returned, and urged Zhiwen to enter court; the Deposed Emperor comforted him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chong reached the capital; the Deposed Emperor had already taken the throne. Chong presented congratulations at once, returned, and urged Zhiwen to court. The Deposed Emperor received him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 知溫還鎮，封東平王。

translations.literal: Zhiwen returned to his post and was enfeoffed Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen returned to his post and was made Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 太常上言：「策拜王公，皇帝臨軒遣冊。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: “In conferring investiture on princes, the emperor faces the hall and dispatches the patent.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: “To invest princes, the emperor faces the hall and dispatches the patent.

sentences.zh: 其在外者，正衙命使，而鹵簿、鼓吹、輅車、法物不出都城，考之故事無明文。

translations.literal: For those outside, the main court orders envoys, yet the guard of honor, music, imperial carriage, and ritual objects do not leave the capital; searching the precedents, there is no clear text.
translations.idiomatic: For those outside, the main court sends envoys—but guard of honor, music, imperial carriage, and ritual objects do not leave the capital; precedents have no clear text.

sentences.zh: 今北平王德鈞、東平王知溫受封遣策，請下兵部、太常、太僕，給鹵簿、鼓吹、輅車、法物赴本道，禮畢還有司。

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Beiping, Dejun, and the Prince of Dongping, Zhiwen, receive patents by dispatch—please order the Ministry of War, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and the Imperial Stud to supply guard of honor, music, carriage, and ritual objects to their circuits; when the rite is done, return them to the proper offices.
translations.idiomatic: Now Prince of Beiping Dejun and Prince of Dongping Zhiwen receive patents by dispatch—order War, Sacrifices, and the Imperial Stud to send guard of honor, music, carriage, and ritual objects to their circuits; when the rite ends, return them to the proper offices.

sentences.zh: 」知溫在鎮，常厚斂其民，積貲巨萬，治第青州南城，出入以聲妓，遊嬉不恤政事。

translations.literal: In his post Zhiwen often levied heavily on the people, amassed wealth in the tens of millions, built a mansion in Qingzhou’s south city, went out with singing girls, and played without caring for government.
translations.idiomatic: In his post Zhiwen taxed the people hard, amassed tens of millions, built a mansion in Qingzhou’s south city, went out with singing girls, and played while government rotted.

sentences.zh: 天福元年卒於宮，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianfu he died in his residence and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu 1: he died at his residence and was made Grand Marshal posthumously.

sentences.zh: 知溫卒後，其子彥儒獻其父錢三萬緡、絹布三萬匹、金百兩、銀千兩、茶千五百斤、絲十萬兩，拜沂州刺史。

translations.literal: After Zhiwen died, his son Yanru presented his father’s money of thirty thousand strings, silk cloth thirty thousand bolts, gold a hundred taels, silver a thousand taels, tea fifteen hundred jin, and silk a hundred thousand liang, and was made prefect of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhiwen died, his son Yanru presented his father’s thirty thousand strings of cash, thirty thousand bolts of silk, a hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, fifteen hundred jin of tea, and a hundred thousand liang of silk, and was made prefect of Yi.

sentences.zh: 其將吏分其餘貲者，皆為富家云。

translations.literal: His generals and clerks who divided the rest of the wealth all became rich households, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His generals and clerks who split the rest of the hoard all became rich men, it is said.

sentences.zh: ○王晏球

translations.literal: ○ Wang Yanqiu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanqiu

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，遷龍驤四軍指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Yanqiu was moved to commander of the four Dragon-Prancing armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Yanqiu was made commander of the four Dragon-Prancing armies.

sentences.zh: 梁遣捉生軍將李霸將千人戍楊劉，霸夜作亂，自水門入，縱火大噪，以長竿縛布沃油，仰燒建國門。

translations.literal: Liang sent the captive-recruiting general Li Ba with a thousand men to garrison Yangliu; Ba mutinied by night, entered through the water gate, set fires and raised a great clamor, and with long poles bound cloth soaked in oil and burned it upward against the Jianguo Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Li Ba of the captive-recruiting corps with a thousand men to garrison Yangliu. Ba mutinied at night, came in through the water gate, set fires and roared, bound oil-soaked cloth to long poles, and burned upward at the Jianguo Gate.

sentences.zh: 晏球聞亂，不俟命，率龍驤五百騎擊之，賊勢稍卻。

translations.literal: Yanqiu heard the uproar, did not wait for orders, and led five hundred Dragon-Prancing horsemen to strike; the rebels’ force slightly fell back.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu heard the uproar, waited for no order, and led five hundred Dragon-Prancing horse to strike. The rebels fell back a little.

sentences.zh: 末帝登樓見之，呼曰：「此非吾龍驤軍邪！

translations.literal: The Last Emperor climbed the tower and saw it, and called out: “Are these not my Dragon-Prancing troops!
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor climbed the tower, saw them, and called: “Are these not my Dragon-Prancing troops!

sentences.zh: 」晏球奏曰：「亂者，李霸一部爾，陛下嚴守宮城，而責臣破賊。

translations.literal: ” Yanqiu reported: “The mutineers are only Li Ba’s unit; Your Majesty, hold the palace fast and charge me to break the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yanqiu reported: “The mutineers are only Li Ba’s band. Your Majesty, hold the palace fast and charge me to break them.

sentences.zh: 」遲明盡殺之，以功拜澶州刺史。

translations.literal: ” At dawn he had killed them all; for merit he was made prefect of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: ” By dawn he had killed them all. For merit he was made prefect of Cao.

sentences.zh: 梁、晉軍河上，以晏球為行營馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Liang and Jin armies faced each other on the river; Yanqiu was made commander-in-chief of the campaign’s horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Jin faced each other on the river. Yanqiu was made commander-in-chief of the campaign horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，晏球以兵追之，行至封丘，聞末帝已崩，即解甲降唐，莊宗賜姓名曰李紹虔，拜齊州防禦使，戍瓦橋關。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong entered Bian; Yanqiu pursued with troops, reached Fengqiu, heard the Last Emperor had fallen, at once doffed armor and surrendered to Tang; Zhuangzong bestowed the surname and personal name Li Shaoqian, made him defense commissioner of Qi, and garrisoned Waqiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong entered Bian. Yanqiu pursued to Fengqiu, heard the Last Emperor was dead, doffed armor and surrendered to Tang. Zhuangzong gave him the name Li Shaoqian, made him defense commissioner of Qi, and garrisoned Waqiao Pass.

sentences.zh: 明宗兵變，自鄴而南，遣人招晏球，晏球從至洛陽，拜歸德軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Mingzong’s troops mutinied and marched south from Ye, he sent men to summon Yanqiu; Yanqiu followed to Luoyang and was made military governor of the Guide army.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong’s troops mutinied and marched south from Ye, he sent for Yanqiu. Yanqiu followed to Luoyang and was made military governor of Guide.

sentences.zh: 定州王都反，以晏球為招討使，與宣徽南院使張延朗等討之。

translations.literal: Wang Du of Dingzhou rebelled; Yanqiu was made pacification commissioner, and with the Southern Court of the Palace Directorate’s Zhang Yanlang and others campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Du of Dingzhou rebelled. Yanqiu was made pacification commissioner and campaigned against him with Zhang Yanlang of the Southern Court and others.

sentences.zh: 都遣人北招契丹，契丹遣禿餒將萬騎救都。

translations.literal: Du sent men north to summon the Khitan; the Khitan sent Tujie with ten thousand horse to rescue Du.
translations.idiomatic: Du sent north for the Khitan. They sent Tujie with ten thousand horse to save him.

sentences.zh: 晏球聞禿餒等兵且來，留張延朗屯新樂，自逆於望都。

translations.literal: Yanqiu heard Tujie’s troops were coming, left Zhang Yanlang encamped at Xinle, and himself went to meet them at Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu heard Tujie was near. He left Zhang Yanlang at Xinle and went to meet him at Wangdu.

sentences.zh: 而契丹從他道入定州，與都出不意擊延朗軍，延朗大敗，收餘兵會晏球趨曲陽，都乘勝追之。

translations.literal: But the Khitan came by another road into Dingzhou, joined Du, and struck Yanlang’s army by surprise; Yanlang was badly defeated, gathered the remnant and joined Yanqiu toward Quyang, and Du pursued in victory.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan came by another road into Dingzhou, joined Du, and struck Yanlang by surprise. Yanlang was routed, gathered the remnant, and joined Yanqiu toward Quyang. Du pursued in victory.

sentences.zh: 晏球先至水次，方坐胡床指麾，而都眾掩至，晏球與左右十餘人連矢射之，都眾稍卻，而後軍亦至。

translations.literal: Yanqiu reached the river first and was just sitting on a camp chair giving orders when Du’s masses closed in; Yanqiu and a dozen or so at his side shot arrows in succession, Du’s masses fell back a little, and then the rear guard also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu reached the river first and sat on a camp chair giving orders when Du’s masses closed in. Yanqiu and a dozen at his side shot in succession. Du’s men fell back a little; then the rear guard came up.

sentences.zh: 晏球立高岡，號令諸將皆橐弓矢、用短兵，回顧者斬。

translations.literal: Yanqiu stood on a high hill and ordered all the generals to case bow and arrow and use short weapons—whoever looked back was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu stood on a high hill and ordered every general to case bow and arrow and fight with short steel—whoever looked back was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 符彥卿以左軍攻其左，高行珪以右軍攻其右，中軍騎士抱馬項馳入都軍，都遂大敗，自曲陽至定州，橫屍棄甲六十餘里。

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing with the left wing struck their left; Gao Xinggui with the right wing struck their right; the center’s horsemen hugged their horses’ necks and charged into Du’s army; Du was utterly defeated, and from Quyang to Dingzhou corpses and cast armor lay across more than sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing struck their left; Gao Xinggui their right. Center horse hugged their mounts’ necks and charged into Du’s host. Du was routed. From Quyang to Dingzhou corpses and cast armor lay across more than sixty li.

sentences.zh: 都與禿餒入城，不敢復出。

translations.literal: Du and Tujie entered the city and did not dare come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Du and Tujie entered the city and did not dare come out again.

sentences.zh: 契丹又遣惕隱以七千騎益都，晏球遇之唐河，追擊至滿城，斬首二千級，獲馬千匹。

translations.literal: The Khitan again sent Tiyin with seven thousand horse to reinforce Du; Yanqiu met them on the Tang River, pursued to Mancheng, and cut off two thousand heads and took a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent Tiyin with seven thousand horse to reinforce Du. Yanqiu met them on the Tang River, pursued to Mancheng, and took two thousand heads and a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 契丹自中國多故，強於北方，北方諸夷無大小皆畏伏，而中國之兵遭契丹者，未嘗少得志。

translations.literal: The Khitan, because China had many troubles, were strong in the north; all northern tribes great and small feared and submitted, yet Chinese troops who met the Khitan had never had much success.
translations.idiomatic: China’s troubles made the Khitan strong in the north; every northern tribe feared them. Chinese troops who met the Khitan had rarely had their way.

sentences.zh: 自晏球擊敗禿餒，又走惕隱，其餘眾奔潰投村落，村落之人以鋤耰白梃所在擊殺之，無復遺類。

translations.literal: From Yanqiu’s defeat of Tujie and rout of Tiyin, the rest scattered and fled into villages; village folk with hoes, flails, and white staves struck and killed them wherever they met, until none were left.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu broke Tujie and routed Tiyin. The rest fled into villages. Villagers with hoes, flails, and white staves killed them wherever they met until none were left.

sentences.zh: 惕隱與數十騎走至幽州西，為趙德鈞擒送京師。

translations.literal: Tiyin and several dozen horsemen fled west of Youzhou and were seized by Zhao Dejun and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tiyin and several dozen horse fled west of Youzhou. Zhao Dejun seized them and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明宗下詔責誚契丹。

translations.literal: Mingzong issued an edict rebuking the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong issued an edict rebuking the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 契丹後數遣使至中國，求歸惕隱等，辭甚卑遜，輒斬其使以絕之。

translations.literal: The Khitan later several times sent envoys to China asking return of Tiyin and the rest; their words were very humble and submissive, yet each time the envoys were beheaded to cut off relations.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan later sent envoys again and again asking return of Tiyin and the rest, humble and submissive. Each envoy was beheaded to cut off relations.

sentences.zh: 於是時，中國之威幾於大震，而契丹少衰伏矣，自晏球始也。

translations.literal: At that time China’s prestige nearly shook the realm, and the Khitan somewhat weakened and submitted—it began with Yanqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Then China’s prestige nearly shook the realm and the Khitan weakened and submitted. It began with Yanqiu.

sentences.zh: 晏球攻定州，久不克，明宗數遣人促其破賊，晏球以謂未可急攻。

translations.literal: Yanqiu besieged Dingzhou long without taking it; Mingzong several times sent men to urge him to break the rebels, but Yanqiu held that a rush attack would not do.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu besieged Dingzhou long without taking it. Mingzong urged him again and again. Yanqiu held that a rush would not do.

sentences.zh: 其偏將朱弘昭、張虔釗等宣言曰：「晏球怯耳！

translations.literal: His deputies Zhu Hongzhao and Zhang Qianzhao and others proclaimed: “Yanqiu is only timid!
translations.idiomatic: His deputies Zhu Hongzhao and Zhang Qianzhao proclaimed: “Yanqiu is only timid!

sentences.zh: 」乃驅兵以進，兵果敗，殺傷三千餘人，由是諸將不敢復言攻。

translations.literal: ” They drove the army forward; the army was indeed defeated, more than three thousand killed and wounded, and from then the generals did not dare speak of attacking again.
translations.idiomatic: ” They drove the army forward. It was routed—more than three thousand killed and wounded. After that no general dared speak of attacking again.

sentences.zh: 晏球乃休養士卒，食其三州之賦，悉以俸祿所入具牛酒，日與諸將高會。

translations.literal: Yanqiu then rested and nourished the troops, fed them on the tax of three prefectures, and spent all his salary income on oxen and wine, daily holding high feasts with the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu rested and fed his men on the tax of three prefectures, spent every cash of salary on oxen and wine, and daily feasted the generals.

sentences.zh: 久之，都城中食盡，先出其民萬餘人，數與禿餒謀決圍以走，不果，都將馬讓能以城降，都自焚死。

translations.literal: After a long while food in the city was exhausted; they first sent out more than ten thousand civilians, several times plotted with Tujie to break the siege and flee, but could not succeed; Du’s officer Ma Rangneng surrendered the city, and Du burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Long after, the city ran out of food. They sent out more than ten thousand civilians, plotted with Tujie several times to break out, and failed. Du’s officer Ma Rangneng surrendered the city. Du burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 晏球為將有機略，善撫士卒。

translations.literal: As a general Yanqiu had stratagem and was skilled at comforting troops.
translations.idiomatic: As a general Yanqiu had stratagem and knew how to comfort troops.

sentences.zh: 其擊禿餒，既因敗以為功，而諸將皆欲乘勝取都，晏球返，獨不動，卒以持久弊之。

translations.literal: In striking Tujie he had turned defeat into merit, yet all the generals wished to press the victory and take Du; Yanqiu returned and alone did not move, and in the end wore them down by endurance.
translations.idiomatic: He had turned defeat into merit against Tujie, yet every general wanted to press on and take Du. Yanqiu held back alone and in the end wore them down by waiting.

sentences.zh: 自天成三年四月都反，明年二月始克之，軍中未嘗戮一人。

translations.literal: From Du’s rebellion in the fourth month of Tiancheng 3 until the city fell in the second month of the next year, not one man was executed in the army.
translations.idiomatic: From Du’s rebellion in Tiancheng 3, month 4, until the city fell in month 2 of the next year, the army executed not one man.

sentences.zh: 以破都功，拜天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: For the merit in breaking Du he was made military governor of the Tianping army.
translations.idiomatic: For breaking Du he was made military governor of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 又徙平盧，累官至兼中書令。

translations.literal: He was again moved to Pinglu and in succession reached concurrent Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Pinglu and rose to concurrent Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 是歲卒，年六十二，贈太尉。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged sixty-two, and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died at sixty-two, posthumously Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 安重霸

translations.literal: An Zhongba
translations.idiomatic: An Zhongba

sentences.zh: 安重霸，雲州人也，初與明宗俱事晉王。

translations.literal: An Zhongba was a man of Yunzhou; in youth he and Mingzong both served the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: An Zhongba came from Yunzhou. In youth he and Mingzong both served the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 重霸得罪奔於梁，又奔於蜀。

translations.literal: Zhongba offended, fled to Liang, and again fled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongba offended, fled to Liang, then fled again to Shu.

sentences.zh: 重霸為人狡譎多智，善事人。

translations.literal: Zhongba was sly and full of schemes, skilled at winning people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongba was sly, full of schemes, and skilled at winning people.

sentences.zh: 蜀王建以為親將。

translations.literal: Shu’s Wang Jian made him a personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shu’s Wang Jian made him a personal guard.

sentences.zh: 王衍立，少年，宦者王承休用事，重霸深結承休以自托。

translations.literal: When Wang Yan rose, he was young; the eunuch Wang Chengxiu held power, and Zhongba bonded deeply with Chengxiu to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yan rose he was young. The eunuch Wang Chengxiu held power. Zhongba bonded deeply with Chengxiu to secure himself.

sentences.zh: 梁末，蜀取李茂貞秦、成、階三州，重霸勸承休求鎮秦州，衍以承休為節度使，重霸為其副使。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, Shu took Li Maozhen’s three prefectures Qin, Cheng, and Jie; Zhongba urged Chengxiu to seek command of Qin, and Yan made Chengxiu military commissioner with Zhongba as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At Liang’s end Shu took Li Maozhen’s Qin, Cheng, and Jie. Zhongba urged Chengxiu to seek Qin. Yan made Chengxiu military commissioner and Zhongba his deputy.

sentences.zh: 重霸與承休多取秦州花木獻衍，請衍東遊。

translations.literal: Zhongba and Chengxiu took many flowers and trees of Qin to present to Yan and asked Yan to tour east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongba and Chengxiu sent Qin’s flowers and trees to Yan and asked him to tour east.

sentences.zh: 唐魏王兵伐蜀，承休大恐，以問重霸，重霸曰：「劍門天下之險，雖有精兵，不可過也。

translations.literal: Tang’s Prince of Wei campaigned against Shu; Chengxiu was greatly afraid and asked Zhongba; Zhongba said: “Jianmen is the world’s peril; though there be elite troops, they cannot pass.
translations.idiomatic: Tang’s Prince of Wei marched on Shu. Chengxiu was terrified and asked Zhongba. Zhongba said: “Jianmen is the world’s peril. Elite troops cannot pass.

sentences.zh: 然公受國恩，聞難不可不赴，願與公俱西。

translations.literal: Yet you have received the state’s grace; hearing trouble you cannot fail to go—I wish to go west with you.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have the state’s grace. Hearing trouble you cannot stay away. I wish to go west with you.

sentences.zh: 」承休素親信之，以為然。

translations.literal: ” Chengxiu had long trusted him and thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chengxiu had long trusted him and agreed.

sentences.zh: 承休整軍將發，秦人送之，帳飲城外。

translations.literal: Chengxiu arrayed the army to set out; the people of Qin saw them off with a tent feast outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu arrayed the army to march. The people of Qin saw them off with a tent feast outside the wall.

sentences.zh: 酒罷，承休上道，重霸立承休馬前，辭曰：「秦、隴不可失，願留為公守。

translations.literal: When the wine was done Chengxiu took the road; Zhongba stood before Chengxiu’s horse and declined: “Qin and Long cannot be lost—I beg to remain and guard for you.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was done Chengxiu took the road. Zhongba stood before his horse and declined: “Qin and Long cannot be lost. Let me remain and guard for you.

sentences.zh: 」承休業已上道，無如之何。

translations.literal: ” Chengxiu had already set out and could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chengxiu had already set out and could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 唐軍已破蜀，重霸亦以秦、成、階三州降唐，明宗以為閬州團練使。

translations.literal: Tang’s army had already broken Shu; Zhongba also surrendered the three prefectures Qin, Cheng, and Jie to Tang, and Mingzong made him regimental commissioner of Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang had already broken Shu. Zhongba surrendered Qin, Cheng, and Jie to Tang. Mingzong made him regimental commissioner of Lang.

sentences.zh: 罷為左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was removed to senior general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed to senior general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 久之，以為匡國軍節度使。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made military governor of the Kuangguo army.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was made military governor of Kuangguo.

sentences.zh: 廢帝時，為京兆尹、西京留守，徙鎮大同，以病罷還，卒於潞州。

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor he was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and western capital regent, was moved to hold Datong, was removed for illness and returned, and died at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor he was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and western capital regent, moved to Datong, removed for illness, returned, and died at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 王建立

translations.literal: Wang Jianli
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jianli

sentences.zh: 建立與安重誨素不協，定州王都有二誌，數以書通建立，約為兄弟，重誨知之以為言。

translations.literal: Jianli and An Chonghui had long been at odds; Wang Du of Dingzhou had two minds and several times wrote Jianli, pledging brotherhood; Chonghui learned of it and spoke against him.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli and An Chonghui had long been at odds. Wang Du of Dingzhou wavered and wrote Jianli again and again, pledging brotherhood. Chonghui learned of it and spoke against him.

sentences.zh: 明宗不欲傷建立，亟召還京師。

translations.literal: Mingzong did not wish to harm Jianli and urgently summoned him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong did not wish to harm Jianli and urgently summoned him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 建立入見，亦多言重誨過失。

translations.literal: Jianli entered audience and also spoke much of Chonghui’s faults.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli entered audience and spoke much of Chonghui’s faults.

sentences.zh: 明宗大怒，欲亟罷重誨，群臣左右諷解之，乃止。

translations.literal: Mingzong was greatly angry and wished at once to remove Chonghui; ministers left and right urged and explained, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was furious and meant to remove Chonghui at once. Ministers urged and explained; he stopped.

sentences.zh: 然卒以建立為右僕射、同中書門下平章事、判三司事。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Jianli was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, co–Grand Councillor, and overseer of the Three Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end Jianli was made Right Vice Director, co–Grand Councillor, and overseer of the Three Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 居歲餘，自言不識文字，願解三司，明宗不許。

translations.literal: After more than a year he said himself he did not know writing and wished to be relieved of the Three Bureaus; Mingzong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he said he could not read and wished to leave the Three Bureaus. Mingzong would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 久之，建立稱疾，明宗笑曰：「人固有詐疾而得疾者。

translations.literal: After a long while Jianli claimed illness; Mingzong laughed: “Men indeed feign illness and thereby fall ill.
translations.idiomatic: Long after, Jianli claimed illness. Mingzong laughed: “Men feign illness and thereby fall ill.

sentences.zh: 」乃出為平盧節度使，又徙上黨。

translations.literal: ” He was sent out as military governor of Pinglu, then moved to Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was sent out as military governor of Pinglu, then moved to Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 建立怏怏不得志，遂求解職，乃以太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: Jianli was resentful and without success, then sought to resign office, and was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli was resentful and sought release. He was made Junior Mentor of the Heir and retired.

sentences.zh: 建立數請朝見，不許，乃自詣京師，闌至後樓見明宗，涕泣言己無罪，為重誨所擯，明宗曰：「汝為節度使，不作好事，豈獨重誨讒汝邪！

translations.literal: Jianli several times asked to attend court and was not permitted; he then went on his own to the capital, forced his way to the rear tower to see Mingzong, wept and said he was guiltless and had been slandered by Chonghui; Mingzong said: “You were a military commissioner and did no good—was it only Chonghui who slandered you!
translations.idiomatic: Jianli asked again and again to attend court and was refused. He went on his own to the capital, forced his way to the rear tower, wept, and said he was guiltless and slandered by Chonghui. Mingzong said: “You were a military commissioner and did no good—was it only Chonghui who slandered you!

sentences.zh: 」賜以茶藥而遣之。

translations.literal: ” He was given tea and medicine and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was given tea and medicine and sent away.

sentences.zh: 廢帝立，復起為天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne Jianli was again raised as military governor of the Tianping army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne Jianli was raised again as military governor of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時，徙鎮平盧。

translations.literal: Under Jin’s Gaozu he was moved to hold Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s Gaozu he was moved to Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 天福五年來朝，高祖勞之曰：「三十年前老兄，可毋拜！

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu he came to court; Gaozu comforted him: “Thirty years ago, old brother—you need not bow!
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 5 he came to court. Gaozu comforted him: “Thirty years ago, old brother—you need not bow!

sentences.zh: 」賜以肩輿入朝，給二宦者掖而升殿，宴見甚渥。

translations.literal: ” He was granted a shoulder carriage for court entry, two eunuchs to support him up the hall, and the feast audience was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was granted a shoulder carriage for court, two eunuchs to support him up the hall, and the feast audience was lavish.

sentences.zh: 又徙昭義，賜以玉斧、蜀馬。

translations.literal: He was again moved to Zhaoyi and given a jade axe and a Shu horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved again to Zhaoyi and given a jade axe and a Shu horse.

sentences.zh: 累封韓王。

translations.literal: In succession he was enfeoffed Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In succession he was enfeoffed Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 建立好殺人，其晚節始惑浮圖法，戒殺生，所至人稍安之。

translations.literal: Jianli loved killing; only in his late years did he turn to Buddhist law, forswore killing, and wherever he went people were somewhat easier.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli loved killing. Only in late years did he turn to Buddhist law, forswore killing, and wherever he went people were somewhat easier.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十，贈尚書令。

translations.literal: He died aged seventy and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy, posthumously Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 守恩性貪鄙，人甚苦之。

translations.literal: Shou’en was greedy and base; people suffered greatly under him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shou’en was greedy and base; people suffered greatly under him.

sentences.zh: 時周太祖以樞密使將白文珂等軍西平三叛，還過洛陽，守恩以使相自處，肩輿出迎。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou’s Taizu as Bureau of Military Affairs led Bai Wenke’s army and others west to pacify the three rebellions; returning he passed Luoyang, and Shou’en treated himself as envoy-minister, came out in a shoulder carriage to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou’s Taizu, as Bureau of Military Affairs, led Bai Wenke and others west to pacify the three rebellions. Returning through Luoyang, Shou’en treated himself as envoy-minister and came out in a shoulder carriage to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，即日以頭子命文珂代守恩為留守，而守恩方詣館謁，坐於客次以俟見，而吏馳報新留守視事於府矣。

translations.literal: Taizu was angry; that very day with a head-crest token he ordered Wenke to replace Shou’en as regent, while Shou’en was just calling at the guest lodge, sitting in the outer hall awaiting audience, when clerks galloped to report the new regent was already conducting affairs at the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was angry. That very day with a head-crest token he ordered Wenke to replace Shou’en as regent. Shou’en was at the guest lodge, sitting in the outer hall to await audience, when clerks galloped word that the new regent was already conducting affairs at the office.

sentences.zh: 守恩大驚，不知所為，遂罷去，奉朝請於京師。

translations.literal: Shou’en was greatly alarmed, did not know what to do, then resigned and served at court in the capital as a court gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Shou’en was alarmed, knew not what to do, resigned, and served at court in the capital as a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後隱帝殺史弘肇等，召群臣上殿慰諭之，群臣恐懼，無敢言者，獨守恩前對曰：「陛下始睡覺矣。

translations.literal: Later when the Hidden Emperor killed Shi Hongzhao and others he summoned the ministers to the hall to comfort and instruct them; the ministers were afraid and none dared speak; only Shou’en stepped forward and answered: “Your Majesty has only just awakened.
translations.idiomatic: Later when the Hidden Emperor killed Shi Hongzhao and others he summoned ministers to the hall to comfort them. All were afraid; none spoke. Only Shou’en stepped forward: “Your Majesty has only just awakened.

sentences.zh: 」聞者皆縮頭。

translations.literal: ” Hearers all shrank their heads.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hearers all shrank their heads.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，為左金吾衛上將軍以卒。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era he was Left Golden Crow guard senior general and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiande era he was Left Golden Crow guard senior general and died in office.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 道德仁義，所以為治，而法制綱紀，亦所以維持之也。

translations.literal: Virtue, morality, benevolence, and righteousness are what govern; law, institutions, and discipline are also what sustain it.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue, morality, benevolence, and righteousness govern; law, institutions, and discipline sustain them.

sentences.zh: 自古亂亡之國，必先壞其法制而後亂從之。

translations.literal: States that fall to chaos in every age first break their laws and institutions, and then chaos follows.
translations.idiomatic: States that fall to chaos in every age first break their laws and institutions; then chaos follows.

sentences.zh: 亂與壞相乘，至蕩然無復綱紀，則必極於大亂而後返，此勢之然也，五代之際是已。

translations.literal: Chaos and ruin multiply upon each other until discipline is utterly gone, and there must be extreme chaos before return—such is the tendency; the age of the Five Dynasties was exactly this.
translations.idiomatic: Chaos and ruin multiply until discipline is utterly gone; there must be extreme chaos before return. Such is the tendency. The age of the Five Dynasties was exactly this.

sentences.zh: 若文珂、守恩皆位兼將相，漢大臣也，而周太祖以一樞密使頭子易置之，如更戍卒。

translations.literal: Wenke and Shou’en both held rank combining general and minister; they were Han’s great ministers, yet Zhou’s Taizu with one Bureau head-crest token shifted them as easily as changing garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Wenke and Shou’en both held rank combining general and minister—Han’s great ministers—yet Zhou’s Taizu with one Bureau head-crest token shifted them as easily as changing garrison soldiers.

sentences.zh: 是時，太祖與漢未有間隙之端，其無君叛上之志，宜未萌於心，而其所為如此者，何哉？

translations.literal: At that time Taizu and Han had not yet any breach, and the mind to be without a ruler and rebel above had surely not yet sprouted—why then were his acts such?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Han had not yet any breach, and disloyalty had surely not yet sprouted—why then were his acts such?

sentences.zh: 蓋其習為常事，故特發於喜怒頤指之間，而文珂不敢違，守恩不得拒。

translations.literal: Because it had become routine, it burst forth only between anger and pleasure and a nod of the finger—and Wenke did not dare disobey, Shou’en could not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Because it had become routine, it burst forth only between anger, pleasure, and a nod—and Wenke did not dare disobey, Shou’en could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 太祖既處之不疑，而漢廷君臣亦置而不問，其上下安然而不怪者，豈非朝廷法制綱紀壞亂相乘，其來也遠，既極而至於此歟！

translations.literal: Taizu disposed without doubt, and Han’s court ruler and ministers also set it aside without inquiry; above and below were at ease and did not think it strange—is this not because court law and discipline had long been ruined and multiplied, coming from far off, reaching the extreme and arriving here?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu acted without doubt; Han’s ruler and ministers set it aside without inquiry. Above and below were at ease and thought nothing of it—is this not because court law and discipline had long been ruined, coming from far off, reaching the extreme?

sentences.zh: 是以善為天下慮者，不敢忽於微，而常杜其漸也，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Therefore those who plan well for the realm dare not neglect the slight and constantly block the gradual slide—should one not take warning!
translations.idiomatic: Those who plan well for the realm dare not neglect the slight and constantly block the gradual slide. Should one not take warning!

sentences.zh: 康福，蔚州人也，世為軍校。

translations.literal: Kang Fu was a man of Wei prefecture; for generations his family were military officers.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Fu came from Wei prefecture. For generations his family were military officers.

sentences.zh: 福以騎射事晉王為偏將。

translations.literal: Fu with riding and archery served the Prince of Jin as a deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fu with riding and archery served the Prince of Jin as a deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嘗曰：「吾家以羊馬為生，福狀貌類胡人而豐厚，胡宜羊馬。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong once said: “Our house lives by sheep and horses; Fu’s looks resemble a barbarian and he is stout—barbarians suit sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong once said: “Our house lives by sheep and horses. Fu looks like a barbarian and is stout—barbarians suit sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 」乃令福牧馬於相州，為小馬坊使，逾年馬大蕃滋。

translations.literal: ” He therefore had Fu herd horses at Xiangzhou as petty horse-park commissioner; after more than a year the horses greatly multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had Fu herd horses at Xiangzhou as petty horse-park commissioner. After more than a year the herds greatly multiplied.

sentences.zh: 明宗自魏反，兵過相州，福以小坊馬二千匹歸命，明宗軍勢由是益盛。

translations.literal: When Mingzong rebelled from Wei his army passed Xiangzhou; Fu presented two thousand horses of the petty park in submission, and Mingzong’s army’s momentum thereby grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong rebelled from Wei his army passed Xiangzhou. Fu presented two thousand horses of the petty park. Mingzong’s momentum grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 明宗入立，拜飛龍使，領磁州刺史、襄州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne Fu was made Soaring Dragon commissioner, concurrently prefect of Ci and overseer of Xiang’s horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne Fu was made Soaring Dragon commissioner, concurrently prefect of Ci and overseer of Xiang horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 從劉訓討荊南，無功而還。

translations.literal: He followed Liu Xun against Jingnan and returned without merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Liu Xun against Jingnan and returned without merit.

sentences.zh: 福為將無佗能，善諸戎語，明宗嘗召入便殿，訪以外事，福輒為蕃語以對。

translations.literal: As a general Fu had no other ability but was skilled in the various barbarian tongues; Mingzong once summoned him to the private hall and asked about foreign affairs, and Fu always answered in barbarian speech.
translations.idiomatic: As a general Fu had no other gift but barbarian tongues. Mingzong once summoned him to the private hall and asked about foreign affairs. Fu always answered in barbarian speech.

sentences.zh: 樞密使安重誨惡之，常戒福曰：「無妄奏事，當斬汝！

translations.literal: Bureau of Military Affairs An Chonghui hated this and often warned Fu: “Do not memorialize rashly—you will be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Bureau An Chonghui hated it and often warned Fu: “Do not memorialize rashly—you will be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 」福懼，求外任。

translations.literal: ” Fu was afraid and sought an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu was afraid and sought an outside post.

sentences.zh: 靈武韓洙死，第六澄立，而偏將李從賓作亂。

translations.literal: At Lingwu, Han Zhu died; the sixth [son] Cheng was installed, but a deputy general Li Congbin rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingwu Han Zhu died. The sixth son Cheng was set up, but the deputy Li Congbin rebelled.

sentences.zh: 澄表請朝廷命帥，而重誨以謂靈武深入夷境，為帥者多遇害，乃拜福涼州刺史，朔方、河西軍節度使。

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized asking the court to appoint a commander; Chonghui held that Lingwu lay deep in barbarian territory and commanders there often perished, and therefore Fu was made prefect of Liangzhou and military commissioner of Shuofang and Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng asked the court for a commander. Chonghui said Lingwu lay deep in barbarian country and its commanders often died—so Fu was made Liangzhou prefect and commissioner of Shuofang and Hexi.

sentences.zh: 福入見明宗，涕泣言為重誨所擠。

translations.literal: Fu entered to see Mingzong and wept, saying Chonghui had squeezed him out.
translations.idiomatic: Fu came before Mingzong in tears and said Chonghui had forced him out.

sentences.zh: 明宗召重誨為福更佗鎮，重誨曰：「福為刺史無功效而建節旄，其敢有所擇邪！

translations.literal: Mingzong summoned Chonghui to give Fu another circuit; Chonghui said: “Fu became prefect with no merit and was given a commissioner’s banner—how dare he choose!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong called Chonghui to move Fu elsewhere. Chonghui said: “Fu was a prefect with no merit and got a commissioner’s banner—how dare he pick and choose!

sentences.zh: 」明宗怒，謂福曰：「重誨遣汝，非吾意也。

translations.literal: ” Mingzong grew angry and told Fu: “Chonghui sent you—not my intent.
translations.idiomatic: ” Mingzong flared up and told Fu: “Chonghui sent you—not my wish.

sentences.zh: 吾當遣兵護汝，可無憂。

translations.literal: I will send troops to escort you; you need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: I will send troops to guard you—fear nothing.

sentences.zh: 」乃令將軍牛知柔以兵衛福。

translations.literal: ” He thereupon ordered General Niu Zhirou to guard Fu with troops.
translations.idiomatic: ” He ordered General Niu Zhirou to escort Fu with troops.

sentences.zh: 行至方渠，而羌夷果出邀福，福以兵擊走之。

translations.literal: When he reached Fangqu, the Qiang and Yi indeed came out to intercept Fu; Fu drove them off with troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Fangqu the Qiang and Yi came out to waylay him as expected; Fu beat them off.

sentences.zh: 至青岡峽，遇雪，福登山望見川谷中煙火，有吐蕃數千帳，不覺福至，福分其兵馬三道，出其不意襲之。

translations.literal: At Qinggang Gorge he met snow; Fu climbed a hill and saw smoke in the valley—several thousand Tibetan tents; they did not know Fu had arrived; Fu split his horse and foot three ways and struck by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinggang Gorge snow fell. Fu climbed a hill, saw smoke in the valley—thousands of Tibetan tents. They did not know he was near. He split his force three ways and struck by surprise.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大駭，棄車帳而走，殺之殆盡，獲其玉璞、綾錦、羊馬甚眾，由是威聲大振。

translations.literal: The Tibetans were greatly alarmed, abandoned carts and tents and fled; nearly all were killed; he took much jade, brocade, sheep, and horses; his fame thereby shook the region.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans panicked, dropped carts and tents, and ran. Nearly all were killed. He took jade, brocade, sheep, and horses in great quantity—and his name shook the frontier.

sentences.zh: 福居靈武三歲，歲常豐稔，有馬千駟，蕃夷畏服。

translations.literal: Fu held Lingwu three years; harvests were yearly full; he had a thousand teams of horses; the barbarians feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fu held Lingwu three years. Harvests ran full every year. He had a thousand teams of horses. The tribes feared and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 言事者疑福有異志，重誨亦言福必負朝廷。

translations.literal: Memorialists suspected Fu of disloyal intent; Chonghui also said Fu would surely betray the court.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists suspected Fu of other designs. Chonghui too said Fu would turn on the court.

sentences.zh: 明宗遣人謂福曰：「我何少汝而欲負我！

translations.literal: Mingzong sent someone to tell Fu: “How have I slighted you that you would betray me!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent word: “How have I wronged you that you would betray me!

sentences.zh: 」福言：「受國恩深，有死無二。

translations.literal: ” Fu said: “I have received deep grace from the state—death without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu said: “The state has favored me deeply—I die without a second thought.

sentences.zh: 」因乞還朝，不許。

translations.literal: ” He therefore begged to return to court; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: ” He begged to return to court and was refused.

sentences.zh: 福章再上，即隨而至，明宗不之罪，徙鎮彰義。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized again and followed straight after; Mingzong did not punish him and moved him to Zhangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu memorialized again and came in person right after. Mingzong did not punish him and moved him to Zhangyi.

sentences.zh: 歷靜難、雄武，充西面都部署。

translations.literal: He passed through Jingnan and Xiongwu and served as western frontier chief of deployment.
translations.idiomatic: He held Jingnan and Xiongwu in turn and served as western frontier chief of deployment.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時，徙鎮河中，代還，卒於京師，贈太師，謚曰武安。

translations.literal: Under Jin’s Gaozu he was moved to hold Hezhong; replaced and recalled; he died in the capital and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, posthumous title Martial Peace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s Gaozu he was moved to Hezhong. Recalled on replacement, he died in the capital and was made Grand Preceptor posthumously, styled Martial Peace.

sentences.zh: 福世本夷狄，夷狄貴沙陀，故常自言沙陀種也。

translations.literal: Fu’s family were originally barbarians; barbarians prized the Shatuo, so he often said he was of Shatuo stock.
translations.idiomatic: Fu’s line was barbarian stock; barbarians prized the Shatuo, so he often called himself Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 福嘗有疾臥閣中，寮佐入問疾，見其錦衾，相顧竊戲曰：「錦衾爛兮！

translations.literal: Fu was once ill in his pavilion; aides came to inquire and saw his brocade quilt; they glanced at each other and whispered in jest: “The brocade quilt rots!
translations.idiomatic: Fu once lay ill in his pavilion. Aides came to ask after him, saw his brocade quilt, and whispered to each other in jest: “The brocade quilt rots!

sentences.zh: 」福聞之，怒曰：「我沙陀種也，安得謂我為奚？

translations.literal: ” Fu heard, grew angry, and said: “I am Shatuo stock—how dare you call me Xi!
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu heard and raged: “I am Shatuo—how dare you call me Xi!

sentences.zh: 」聞者笑之。

translations.literal: ” Those who heard laughed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Those who heard laughed.

sentences.zh: 郭延魯

translations.literal: Guo Yanlu
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yanlu

sentences.zh: 郭延魯，沁州綿上人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yanlu came from Mianshang in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yanlu came from Mianshang in Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 父饒，以驍勇事晉，數立軍功，為沁州刺史者九年，為政有惠愛，州人思之。

translations.literal: His father Rao, for valor served Jin, won battle merit repeatedly, held Qin as prefect nine years, governed with kindness, and the people missed him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rao served Jin for valor, won battle merit again and again, held Qin nine years as prefect, governed with kindness, and the people still missed him.

sentences.zh: 延魯以善槊為將，累遷神武都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Yanlu became a general for skill with the spear and rose to commander of horse and foot in the Divine Martial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlu rose as a general for the spear and became commander of horse and foot in the Divine Martial guard.

sentences.zh: 朱守殷反，從攻汴州，以先登功為汴州馬步軍都指揮使，累遷復州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhu Shouyin rebelled; he followed the attack on Bianzhou, for scaling the walls first was made chief of Bian’s horse and foot, and rose in turn to prefect of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouyin rebelled. He joined the attack on Bianzhou, was first over the wall, made chief of Bian horse and foot, and rose to prefect of Fu.

sentences.zh: 延魯嘆曰：「吾先君為沁州者九年，民到於今思之。

translations.literal: Yanlu sighed: “My late father held Qin nine years—the people still miss him today.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlu sighed: “My father held Qin nine years—the people still miss him.

sentences.zh: 吾今幸得為刺史，其敢忘吾先君之志！

translations.literal: Now I am fortunate to be prefect—how dare I forget my father’s aim!
translations.idiomatic: Now I am prefect by fortune—how dare I forget what he meant to do!

sentences.zh: 」由是益以廉平自勵，民甚賴之。

translations.literal: ” He therefore urged himself more to integrity and fairness; the people relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: ” He pressed himself harder to integrity and fairness, and the people leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，州人乞留，不許，皆遮道攀號。

translations.literal: When his term ended the people begged to keep him; it was denied; all blocked the road weeping and clinging.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended the people begged to keep him. The court refused. They blocked the road, weeping and clinging to him.

sentences.zh: 天福中，拜單州刺史，卒於官。

translations.literal: In Tianfu he was made prefect of Shan and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu he was made Shan prefect and died in his post.

sentences.zh: 當是時，刺史皆以軍功拜，言事者多以為言，以謂方天下多事，民力困敝之時，不宜以刺史任武夫，恃功縱下，為害不細。

translations.literal: At that time prefects were all appointed for military merit; memorialists often spoke on it, saying that when the realm had many troubles and the people’s strength was exhausted, it was unfit to give prefectures to warriors who relied on merit and indulged subordinates—the harm was no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Then every prefect was a man of military merit. Memorialists often said that in a time of troubles, with the people worn thin, warriors should not hold prefectures—relying on merit they indulged subordinates, and the harm was not small.

sentences.zh: 而延魯父子特以善政著聞焉。

translations.literal: Yet the Yanlu father and son were known especially for good government.
translations.idiomatic: Yet father and son Yanlu were known above all for good government.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，五代之民其何以堪之哉！

translations.literal: Alas—how could the people of the Five Dynasties bear it!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how could the people of the Five Dynasties bear it!

sentences.zh: 上輸兵賦之急，下困剝斂之苛。

translations.literal: Above, the urgency of supplying armies and taxes; below, the hardship of harsh exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Above, armies and taxes pressed in; below, stripping and levies crushed them.

sentences.zh: 自莊宗以來，方鎮進獻之事稍作，至於晉而不可勝紀矣。

translations.literal: Since Zhuangzong, circuit tribute had slightly increased; by Jin it could not be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhuangzong, circuit tribute had begun to grow; by Jin it could not all be counted.

sentences.zh: 其「添都」、「助國」之物，動以千數計。

translations.literal: Items called “adding to the capital” and “aiding the state” ran to thousands at a time.
translations.idiomatic: “Adding to the capital” and “aiding the state” goods ran to thousands at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 至於來朝、奉使、買宴、贖罪，莫不出於進獻。

translations.literal: Court visits, missions, buying banquets, redeeming crimes—all came from tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Court visits, missions, buying banquets, redeeming crimes—all came out of tribute.

sentences.zh: 而功臣大將，不幸而死，則其子孫率以家貲求刺史，其物多者得大州善地。

translations.literal: When great merit officers died, their sons and grandsons commonly used family wealth to seek prefectures; those with more goods got large provinces and good lands.
translations.idiomatic: When great officers died, their sons and grandsons commonly bought prefectures with family wealth—the richer the gift, the larger the province and the better the land.

sentences.zh: 蓋自天子皆以賄賂為事矣，則為其民者其何以堪之哉！

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven down, business was bribery—then how could the people bear it!
translations.idiomatic: From the Son of Heaven down, all was bribery—how could the people bear it!

sentences.zh: 於此之時，循廉之吏如延魯之徒者，誠難得而可貴也哉！

translations.literal: In such a time, upright officials like Yanlu were truly hard to find and precious indeed!
translations.idiomatic: In such a time, upright men like Yanlu were hard to find—and precious when found!
